identity: The opening of the Thousand and One Nights proper — 'حكاية التاجر مع العفريت', 'الليلة الأولى'. Two heading lines, then one unbroken 419-token paragraph of classical middle-Arabic narrative: Shahrazad's قالت بلغني أيها الملك السعيد frame, the merchant who throws a date-stone and kills the ifrit's son, his year of reprieve, and the arrival of the three old men with the gazelle, the two black saluki bitches and the dappled mule.
law: §O as scoped by batch 13 — un-abridged ADULT classical literary prose, NOT the children's folk tale of doc_a045e64631c7. The batch-2 §O finding stands here and is the governing law: long ف/و event chains are single printed sentences (فسلم … وحياه … وقال، فرجع … وقضى … وأوصل … وأعلم … فبكوا). What ends a sentence in this register is not a connective but a NARRATIVE EVENT closing: the end of a quoted turn, a question, a scene-shift opener (ثم أنه، فبينما، وبينما كذلك، فإذا بشيخ ثان), and the report-clause فأخبره/فأخبراه/فأخبروه. Target unit 15-30 tokens; I landed at 17.5.
reasoning:
The dialogue skeleton gives me my only hi-confidence cuts, and I take all of them: @72 ولدي (end of the ifrit's 'قم حتى أقتلك مثل ما قتلت ولدي'), @78 ولدك (the merchant's question 'كيف قتلت ولدك؟' — T8: a question that IS a complete conversational turn cuts, unlike the verse-internal and MCQ-internal questions that weld), @95 ساعته (end of the ifrit's reply), @139 وكيل (the closing oath of the merchant's plea), @416 كبدي (the ifrit's repeated threat). G1 forbids splitting a speech verb from its quotation, so every فقال/وقال stays welded FORWARD to what it introduces and the boundary falls on the last word of the PREVIOUS turn — that is why @72, not @73, and @95, not @96.
Scene-shift openers @203 (before فبينما هو جالس), @277 and @297 (before each ثم أنه), @318 (before فإذا بشيخ ثان), @171 (before ثم توجه) are the classical narrative's paragraph-level punctuation and I treat them as full stops.
The three-elder passage is near-parallel and I segmented the three blocks the same way: [arrival] / [greeting + question] / [report]. @238 الجن is forced (a direct question with a question mark), and @343 الجان / @370 المكان are its indirect twins, so the six-token 'فأخبراه بالقصة من أولها إلى آخرها' and 'فأخبروه بالقصة من أولها إلى آخرها' each stand as their own printed sentence — short, but that formula is a stock sentence in this text. Elder 1's block runs 48 tokens against 31 and 27 for elders 2 and 3, which is why it alone also takes @220 مسلسلة before فسلم.
My weakest three, all marked lo, are in the opening run 8-72, which would otherwise be 65 tokens — far past this register's ceiling, so something has to break there even though the standard printing of this passage is notoriously comma-chained. @30 البلاد before فاشتد عليه الحر, @45 وتمرة before the fronted فلما (LAW 0''' item 9 puts the cut BEFORE a fronted temporal clause, never after it), @59 سيف before فدنا. @111 رهون is the same kind of bet: it separates the merchant's statement of his affairs from his request فدعني أذهب, which turns a 44-token speech into 16 + 28.
Deliberate WELDS: @159 له before فبكوا — this is §O's protected case, the ف of immediate result as the second beat of one action, so the 32-token فاستوثق…السنة chain stays whole; @303 معه before فغشي, same reason, and cutting it would leave a six-token 'ثم أنه جلس عنده يتحدث معه' that has no event in it; @264 عظيم before وحكايتك حكاية عجيبة — و + NOUN, LAW 1 re-revised, weld; @389 البرية before فانكشفت الغبرة — one continuous storm-description; @161 وكذلك جميع أهله and @265 وحكايتك — coordinated NPs, protected list item 1.
